precepts.text: Simon, Simon, behold, Satan hath desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat: but I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not: and when thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren. Christ is showing Peter that he still has things to work on. Peter answers, Lord, I am ready to go with thee, both into prison, and to death; and Christ says, I tell thee, Peter, the cock shall not crow this day, before that thou shalt thrice deny that thou knowest me. Peter, you are not there yet. And Peter did become the head of the church afterwards, but first there were things he had to reconcile within himself. God opens the book, we behold ourselves in it, and he sends prophets to show us how to get right. The worst thing to do is deny it. Medicine hurts sometimes, but if you are sincere you take your medicine and you get better.
precepts.point: Christ called Simon and Andrew, James and John, from their nets: come ye after me, and I will make you to become fishers of men. These men came in to get right. Do you think that walking with him he was not showing them all their errors?

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
God said, “Behold, I send my messenger before thy face”: John, sent to teach the people and get them right to prepare for Christ. That is the job of the prophet, the apostle and every teacher: to show you. Then Christ called Simon and Andrew, James and John, from their nets. These men came in to get right, and do you think that walking with him he was not showing them all their errors? Luke shows him doing it with Peter.

“And the Lord said, Simon, Simon, behold, Satan hath desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat: But I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not: and when thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren.” When you get right, then go strengthen your brethren. Christ is showing Peter he still has things to work on. You want to walk with me? I'm going to show you what your problems are.

Peter answered, “Lord, I am ready to go with thee, both into prison, and to death.” And Christ said, “I tell thee, Peter”, didn't you just hear what I said to you? “the cock shall not crow this day, before that thou shalt thrice deny that thou knowest me.” Peter, you ain't there yet. Your mind ain't right yet. Get converted first.

Peter did become the head of the church afterwards, but first there were things he had to reconcile within himself. God opens his book and we behold ourselves in it; he sends prophets to show us how to get right. The worst thing to do is deny it. It don't feel good when you're going through it, but it's good for you. Medicine hurts sometimes, but if you are sincere you take your medicine and you get better. If you don't, you become an example of what not to do.

And those who teach must turn it on themselves too: don't weaponize the scriptures to correct everybody else while you can't see your own flaws, or hold brothers to a perfection you yourself are far from.

precepts.text: That ye may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit on thrones doing what? Judging the twelve tribes of Israel. Don't read all this and try to throw Chinese and Japanese and everybody in there. Stop it.
precepts.point: For there are set thrones of judgment, the thrones of the house of David. Pray for the peace of Jerusalem: they shall prosper that love thee. Some of y'all busy praying for Haiti, praying for Puerto Rico, praying for Mexico, praying for America. But the Bible said pray for Jerusalem. Remember, Jerusalem's a people before it's a place. We are Jerusalem. Pray for us. We're not supposed to be praying, stop the war over there; no, we got to move them out of our land so that we can go back home.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
The psalm says that in Jerusalem “there are set thrones of judgment, the thrones of the house of David.” Christ tells his apostles who sits on them and whom they judge: “And I appoint unto you a kingdom, as my Father hath appointed unto me; That ye may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.”

Sit on thrones doing what? Judging the twelve tribes of Israel. The thrones of judgment are for Israel, just as the tribes that go up to Jerusalem are “the tribes of the Lord, unto the testimony of Israel.”

So don't read all this and try to throw the Chinese and the Japanese and everybody in there. Stop it. The kingdom, the table, the thrones and the judgment all belong to the twelve tribes.

precepts.text: The bread which we break, is it not the communion of the body of Christ? For we being many are one bread, and one body: for we are all partakers of that one bread. We are all partakers of that manna.
precepts.point: He took bread, and gave thanks, and brake it, and gave unto them, saying, This is my body which is given for you: this do in remembrance of me.

note.label: Daily Bread for a Dying Man

precepts.why:
Christ “took bread, and gave thanks, and brake it”, and said, “This is my body which is given for you”. Paul shows what that breaking of bread is: “The cup of blessing which we bless, is it not the communion of the blood of Christ? The bread which we break, is it not the communion of the body of Christ?”

“For we being many are one bread, and one body: for we are all partakers of that one bread.” We are all partakers of that manna. Christ is the true manna, the bread from heaven, and we feed upon Christ through his words.

So when we break bread together we are not only eating a piece of bread. We are showing that we are one body, all of us feeding on the same bread, which is Christ and the word of God. That is the fuller sense of “this do in remembrance of me.”

precepts.text: We do this every Sabbath, and here is another reason to take it seriously: the broken bread, the remembrance, the body, the sacrifice, that he is the true manna. You break bread every time we come together, but are you eating the bread that is abundant for us? The breaking of bread is also symbolic of that manna and the commitment we have to consume God's word every day.
precepts.point: He took bread, and gave thanks, and brake it, and gave unto them, saying, This is my body which is given for you: this do in remembrance of me.

note.label: Daily Bread for a Dying Man

precepts.why:
We do this every Sabbath, and here is another reason to take it seriously. Paul received it of the Lord: “the Lord Jesus the same night in which he was betrayed took bread: And when he had given thanks, he brake it, and said, Take, eat: this is my body, which is broken for you: this do in remembrance of me.” Then “This cup is the new testament in my blood: this do ye, as oft as ye drink it, in remembrance of me.”

The broken bread, the remembrance, the body, the sacrifice: he is the true manna. You break bread every time we come together, but are you eating the bread that is abundant for us? Breaking bread once a week and thinking that is all right is not enough. The breaking of bread is also symbolic of that manna and the commitment we have to consume God's word every day, day and night.

Revelation 2:17 promises it: “To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the hidden manna”. The body is dying; you are born and on a path to death. The flesh fights, the mind forgets, and the soul is weighed down by this tabernacle, so the inward man has to be renewed and kept alive by the word daily. The manna showed it, the prophets lived it, David meditated on it, Paul explained it, and Christ revealed himself to be that true bread from heaven. “It is the spirit that quickeneth; the flesh profiteth nothing: the words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life.”

In the wilderness Israel sacrificed daily, twice daily. Psalm 51: “For thou desirest not sacrifice; else would I give it”, but “The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.” If we really considered our ways, our thoughts and our behaviors, we would understand why we need to seek him daily and continually to forgive our sins; feeding yourself so sparingly, you won't understand this.

precepts.text: When thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren.
precepts.point: Think of the faith the Bishop had to have for the truth to be where it is. The impact reaches beyond the purple and gold: outsiders email to donate to the booster club, and every camp watches IUIC at 6 on Saturday night whatever time they teach themselves.

note.label: Mindset Of A Leader, Actions Of A King

precepts.why:
Christ told Peter, “But I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not: and when thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren.” When you convert, strengthen your brothers. That is the charge that goes with the faith that is passed on to you.

Read on and Peter answers, “Lord, I am ready to go with thee, both into prison, and to death”, and Christ answers that before the cock crows Peter will thrice deny that he knows him. Christ prayed that Peter's faith would not fail, knowing what was coming, and still gave him the work of strengthening his brethren.

This is the leader transferring his belief onto others. Christ imparted his faith to Peter, and Peter was to impart it to the brethren. The one who has been strengthened turns around and strengthens the next man.

precepts.text: That ye may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
precepts.point: Look upon Zion, the city of our solemnities; thine eyes shall see Jerusalem a quiet habitation, at rest, a tabernacle that shall not be taken down, not one stake removed nor any cord broken. You will never take down Jerusalem again. Psalms 46:4-7, God is in the midst of her, she shall not be moved; the heathen raged, the kingdoms were moved, he uttered his voice, the earth melted; the God of Jacob is our refuge. Psalms 48:1-2, beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion, the city of the great King.

note.label: Hope Amid Destruction

precepts.why:
Psalms 122:5 says “For there are set thrones of judgment, the thrones of the house of David.” Christ tells his apostles where those thrones are: “That ye may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.”

The thrones in Jerusalem are thrones for judging the twelve tribes. That is why Psalms 122 says it is whither the tribes go up, the tribes of the Lord, unto the testimony of Israel, and not all nations.

So the quiet habitation of Isaiah 33:20, the city of our solemnities, is the seat of the kingdom, with Christ's table and the thrones of the house of David set in it.

precepts.text: Judas, betrayest thou the Son of man with a kiss?
precepts.point: Faithful are the wounds of a friend, but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful.

note.label: Destroyed by Familiar Hands

precepts.why:
“Faithful are the wounds of a friend; but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful.” The last part is the point: the kisses of an enemy are deceitful. And Luke shows the kiss: “Judas, betrayest thou the Son of man with a kiss?” Judas betrayed Christ with a kiss. The man betrayed him with the very sign of love.

Today we do not greet each other with a kiss like that, but we have our own greeting: Shalom, Captain, Most High bless. That is the betrayal. The embrace, the salute, the Shalom, and then the knife. That is the kiss of an enemy.

We saw it in 2018. A man who had been in another man’s house, greeting him with Shalom, barbecuing together, traveling together, came to that same man’s house, took all his furniture and put his children on the cold floor to sleep. He did not care. Not only did he betray the man, he betrayed all his children.

There is nothing worse than a traitor. And some of you think once you betray your brother or your sister, that is the end of it. It is not. The one who betrays with a kiss will be dealt with too. That is why the kisses of an enemy are called deceitful: Judas is the pattern of the familiar hand that destroys.

precepts.text: The feast of unleavened bread drew nigh, which is called the Passover; the two names are one feast.
precepts.point: The feast of harvest, the firstfruits of thy labours, is also known as Pentecost and the feast of weeks; and the feast of ingathering, in the end of the year, is also known as the feast of tabernacles and the feast of booths.

note.label: Exodus 23: Righteous Judgment, the Three Feasts, and the Angel of the Covenant

precepts.why:
“Three times thou shalt keep a feast unto me in the year.” The first is “the feast of unleavened bread”, kept “in the time appointed of the month Abib”, the first month of the year. That feast is the Passover, as it is written: “Now the feast of unleavened bread drew nigh, which is called the Passover.” The two names are one feast.

“and none shall appear before me empty”: you could not come empty-handed. You brought the tenth of your oil, your wine, whatever was required, for the priests to replenish the storehouses.

Next, “the feast of harvest, the firstfruits of thy labours” is also known as Pentecost and the feast of weeks; and “the feast of ingathering, which is in the end of the year” is also known as the feast of tabernacles and the feast of booths. At these three feasts all the males appeared before the Lord God.

precepts.text: The feast of unleavened bread is called the Passover; the two feasts run together as one.
precepts.point: On the last day of unleavened bread you may also cook, unless it falls on the seventh day Sabbath. The only time you can cook on the seventh day Sabbath is when the Passover falls on that day, because you cannot have the Passover without the lamb roast with fire; no other high holy day gives you a set meal, and no other feast overrides the Sabbath cooking prohibition.

note.label: Leviticus 23: The Feasts of the Lord

precepts.why:
“In the fourteenth day of the first month at even is the Lord’s passover. And on the fifteenth day of the same month is the feast of unleavened bread unto the Lord.” The fourteenth day at even means the fifteenth day, so both verses are saying the same thing: the first day of the Passover is also the first day of the feast of unleavened bread.

Luke shows the two run together as one: “Now the feast of unleavened bread drew nigh, which is called the Passover.” The feast of unleavened bread is called the Passover.

On the first day and the seventh day is an holy convocation, no buying, no selling, no servile work. But you can cook on the Passover, because there is no Passover without the Passover meal: the lamb, unleavened bread and bitter herbs.

precepts.text: Satan entered Judas, who communed with the chief priests and covenanted for money to betray Christ in the absence of the multitude.
precepts.point: This is betrayal by someone you know well. Some have suffered these things in the past, and some have suffered them in the truth.

note.label: Psalm 55: Cast Thy Burden Upon the Lord

precepts.why:
At the feast of unleavened bread, the Passover, the chief priests and scribes sought how to kill Christ, “for they feared the people. Then entered Satan into Judas surnamed Iscariot, being of the number of the twelve.” One of the twelve. “And he went his way, and communed with the chief priests and captains, how he might betray him unto them. And they were glad, and covenanted to give him money. And he promised, and sought opportunity to betray him unto them in the absence of the multitude.”

Satan entered a man who was Christ's equal, his acquaintance, of his own company, and he covenanted for money to betray him behind the multitude's back. That is the betrayal of Psalm 55: not an enemy, but one who walked unto the house of God in company. Some have suffered it in the past, and some have suffered it in the truth.

precepts.text: My name is Legion: for we are many. When the unclean spirits were gone out, the man sat clothed, and in his right mind.
precepts.point: The chief priests and captains were glad, and covenanted to give him money. Men are not in their right mind when they can be glad over a thing like that.

note.label: Luke 22: The Passover, the Betrayal, and the Denial

precepts.why:
Satan entered into Judas, one of the twelve, and he went and communed with the chief priests and captains how he might betray him. “And they were glad, and covenanted to give him money.” Men are not in their right mind when they can be glad over a thing like that.

Mark shows what a man looks like when devils are in him and when they are gone. Christ asked the unclean spirit, “What is thy name? And he answered, saying, My name is Legion: for we are many.” The devils begged to go into the swine, and “the herd ran violently down a steep place into the sea, (they were about two thousand;) and were choked in the sea.”

Then the people came “and see him that was possessed with the devil, and had the legion, sitting, and clothed, and in his right mind”. When the unclean spirits were gone out, the man sat clothed and in his right mind. Set that beside the chief priests: Satan had entered Judas, and the men glad to pay for the betrayal of Christ were no more in their right mind than that man was before the legion went out.

precepts.text: I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel, and with the house of Judah.
precepts.point: This cup is the new testament in my blood, which is shed for you. Testament and covenant are the same word, and the scripture names who that covenant was made with.

note.label: Luke 22: The Passover, the Betrayal, and the Denial

precepts.why:
Christ took the cup after supper and said, “This cup is the new testament in my blood, which is shed for you.” Testament and covenant are the same word, and the scripture names who that covenant was made with.

Jeremiah: “Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel, and with the house of Judah”. The new covenant, the new testament in his blood, was promised to the house of Israel and the house of Judah. That is who Christ sat down with at that passover, the twelve apostles, and that is who the blood was shed for.

precepts.text: The same words carried into the new testament: a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah.
precepts.point: This cup is the new testament in my blood, which is shed for you. Testament and covenant are the same word, and the scripture names who that covenant was made with.

note.label: Luke 22: The Passover, the Betrayal, and the Denial

precepts.why:
The same words Jeremiah wrote are carried into the new testament. “For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second. For finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah”.

So the new testament Christ named at the table, in his blood shed for you, is the new covenant of Jeremiah 31, and it is made with the house of Israel and the house of Judah. Jeremiah and Hebrews say the same thing; the covenant did not change who it was made with.

precepts.text: The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul.
precepts.point: Peter walked with him and was not yet converted. What converts a man is named in the psalm, and what he strengthens his brethren with is the same thing.

note.label: Luke 22: The Passover, the Betrayal, and the Denial

precepts.why:
Christ tells Simon that Satan desired to sift him as wheat, “But I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not: and when thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren.” Peter had walked with him all that time and was not yet converted.

The psalm names what converts a man: “The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.” The law of the Lord converts the soul. So when Peter is converted, what he strengthens his brethren with is that same law.

precepts.text: The sting of death is sin; and the strength of sin is the law.
precepts.point: Peter walked with him and was not yet converted. What converts a man is named in the psalm, and what he strengthens his brethren with is the same thing.

note.label: Luke 22: The Passover, the Betrayal, and the Denial

precepts.why:
“The sting of death is sin; and the strength of sin is the law.” Sin is what stings a man to death, and it is the law that gives sin its strength, because the law is what makes it sin. The law is the standard, and the psalm says that same law is perfect, converting the soul.

What converts Peter, and what he strengthens his brethren with when Satan comes to sift them, is the law of the Lord.
